topic: Clearer trade pictures on Telegram (owner: 'they don't show when you bought in, the price, or why'). The owner asked the three AIs to agree; he did not choose.
design: One check-in = one Telegram album: a cover (headline + one row per move with its price) then one card per move, chronological; at most 9 move cards, the cover says how many more.

Each move card: race, date and fill time (ET); headline '<AI> buys/sells/shorts <asset>'; ticker and quantity when known (ChatGPT); boxes for price (with unit), size (with % of the race, from the race's value just before the move) and fill time.
Sells and covers: 'Bought at' / 'Shorted at', or 'Avg entry' when several buys are combined (ChatGPT), with the date of the first buy, the exit price and the result in % and money on that sale.

WHY in the AI's own words, cut at 260 characters with '…', never reworded (Gemini: fixed limit so the chart is not crowded out); WHAT WOULD PROVE IT WRONG (150 characters) on buys, shorts and bets, or 'Not given.'
24-hour price line only when the feed has it; no empty space reserved (ChatGPT). Cards are 1080 wide and 1080 to 1350 tall.
Bets: odds, stake (% of the race), to win; results: stake, result, settled time.
Identical layout, limits, order and data rules for all three AIs, Claude included; a missing number is left out, never estimated.
code: ops/sharecard.py (album, move_card, cover_card, buy_in, race_value, tg_album); used by ops/rivals.py (Gemini, ChatGPT) and ops/telegram.py (Claude)

owner_change.text: Owner: 'make sure descriptive, I like where it explains why'. The why limit went from 260 to 480 characters (wrong-if 150 to 220), long reasons in smaller type; the 24-hour chart is drawn only where it still fits, so the reason always comes first. Same for all three AIs.

owner_change_2.text: Owner: 'for selling, for sure you need to show the buy-in price, when you bought in, how many shares sold; these posts need to be good to grow, not slop'. Sells and covers now lead with THE SALE: units sold of units held (%), units left, the average entry with the date and time of the first buy, the exit price with its date and time, and the result in % and money on that sale; the cover shows units, buy-in, date, exit and % on every sell row. Claude's trades now record qty, held_before, held_after, entry and realized profit (ops/update.py), so its cards show the exact numbers too. Quantity was ChatGPT's must-have and the buy-in was in the proposal all three agreed to.
